extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users learning TikZ/pgf to create diagrams (beginner→intermediate)
extracted.subtask_description: Authoring TikZ/pgf graphics: path construction, styling, transformations, loops, nodes, and text placement for mathematical diagrams and illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectangle path construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the rectangle path construction operation: it should be followed by another coordinate and will append a rectangle to the path such that the previous coordinate and the next coordinate are corners of the rectangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw (0,0) rectangle (1,1); Useful shorthand when rectangles are common, but beware of needing many rectangles and of unclosed borders if misused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grid path construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The grid path operation adds grid lines that fill the rectangle whose one corner is the current point and whose other corner is the following point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: step (uniform grid spacing), xstep and ystep (independent). Example: \draw[step=2pt] (0,0) grid (10pt,10pt); To reduce visual distraction, draw grid first and use subdued color/line width (e.g., gray, very thin or style=help lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use styles for consistent appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and reuse styles (e.g., \tikzstyle help lines=[color=blue!50,very thin]) so that changes to appearance are easy and consistent across the graphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Styles can build on other styles (style=help lines). You can omit the style= prefix; if an unknown option matches a style name, the style is used. Adding style+=[...] appends options (later options override earlier ones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing option: color vs draw
rubrics_metrics.description: color sets a general color option, draw=(color) sets the stroking color and allows a separate fill color to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use draw=... for outline color and fill=... for interior. pgf integrates with xcolor so color expressions like green!20!white work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line thickness naming and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined thickness styles include ultra thin, very thin, thin, semithick, thick, very thick, ultra thick; 'thin' corresponds to a normal line width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use semithick if you need something between thin and thick. Note ultra thin may not render well on low-resolution printers/displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashing and dotting lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Use styles dashed or dotted and their loose/dense variants (loosely dashed, densely dashed, etc.) to create dashed or dotted lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can define complex dash patterns via dash pattern, but use dashing sparingly—overly complex dashes are distracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc path construction syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: The arc operation draws part of a circle or ellipse and must be followed by a triple (start_angle:end_angle:radius).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: arc (10:80:10pt) draws arc from 10° to 80° with radius 10pt. For elliptical arcs specify two radii: arc (0:315:1.75cm and 1cm). The arc starts at the current position, so move the current point first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling whole environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply scaling to entire {tikzpicture} or \tikz by passing [scale=...] to the environment so everything inside is scaled uniformly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better than adding scale= to each \draw. Example: \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=3] ... \end{tikzpicture}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clipping paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \clip to clip all subsequent drawing to the given path; \clip works like \draw but does not draw anything and affects subsequent drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can also combine drawing and clipping with \draw[clip] or \clip[draw]; \path[draw,clip] is the general form. Clipping inside a scope is local to that scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill vs draw vs filldraw
rubrics_metrics.description: \fill fills the path, \draw strokes it, and \filldraw first draws then fills (or vice versa as implemented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use filldraw[fill=...,draw=...] to set different fill and stroke colors. If you forget to close a path, \fill will automatically close it; use --cycle to explicitly close the current part of the path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \shade and \shadedraw for smooth transitions between colors instead of uniform fills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default shading is gray→white. Options include top color, bottom color, left color, right color, inner color, outer color, draw=..., ball color=... Be cautious: shadings often distract without adding value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate specification forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinates may be absolute with units (10pt,2cm), unitless (1,2 meaning multiples of current x- and y-vectors, default 1cm), polar (angle:radius), or relative using + and ++ prefixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polar example: (30:1cm). Unitless coords are scaled by current x/y vectors. +(... ) is relative to the last specified position without changing the 'current specified position'; ++(... ) moves and makes the result the new specified position—use appropriately when repeating shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate intersection shorthand (|- and -|)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (p |- q) to mean the intersection of a vertical line through p and a horizontal line through q (and vice versa with -|).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for projecting coordinates onto axes: (30:1cm |- 0,0) gives the point straight down from (30:1cm) lying on the x-axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: General intersection coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: You can specify intersections of arbitrary segments as coordinates with the syntax (intersection of A--B and C--D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (intersection of 1,0--1,1 and 0,0--30:1cm) finds the intersection point needed for the tan α line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cycle and explicit path closure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use --cycle to close the current part of the path by smoothly joining the first and last point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omitted, filling operations may close the path automatically, but --cycle makes intent explicit and avoids unexpected joins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow tips: adding and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Add arrow tips with ->, <-, or <-> to place tips at the end, start, or both ends of a path respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrow tips are intended for single open lines; adding them to closed shapes (rectangle, circle) is unsupported/undetermined. You can change the tip kind with >=stealth (or other tip names) and define custom tips; many pre-defined kinds exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow-tip restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrow tips generally apply only to single open 'lines'—not guaranteed on closed shapes like rectangles or circles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They can be used on curved paths and multi-segment paths. Expect undefined behaviour if used on shapes not intended for arrow tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping for local options
rubrics_metrics.description: Use {scope} (or \scope/\startscope, \endscope/\stopscope variants) with optional arguments to apply graphic options locally to everything inside the scope but not outside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options given to commands like \draw are 'path options' and can be placed anywhere on the path. Scope also localizes clipping changes: a \clip inside a scope ends at scope end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path option application and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Most graphic options apply to the whole path; if multiple conflicting options are given, the last one wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may write \draw[thin] (0,0) -- (1,0); or \draw (0,0) [thin] -- (1,0); — option placement is flexible. Transformation options are special: they affect only everything following them on the path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformations and mid-path changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Transformation options (xshift, yshift, shift, rotate, rotate around, scale, xscale, yscale, xslant, yslant, cm) modify coordinates in pgf's coordinate system and can be changed in the middle of a path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because pgf maintains its own transformation matrix, mid-path transforms are supported (a feature absent from raw PDF/PostScript). Use cm for arbitrary transformation matrices. Remember transformations only affect subsequent coordinates (not retroactively).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use xshift/yshift/shift for translations
rubrics_metrics.description: xshift and yshift shift subsequent points by given amounts; shift accepts a coordinate (e.g., shift={(1,0)}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with commas in shift (use braces). Transformation options are handy for moving groups of elements without altering coordinates themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: For-loops with \foreach
rubrics_metrics.description: \foreach \var in {list} {commands} iterates over values, assigning \var and executing commands each iteration. If commands don't start with a brace, everything up to the next semicolon is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \foreach \x in {-1,-0.5,1} \draw (\x,-1pt) -- (\x,1pt); Use ... ranges (e.g., {1,...,10}) and two numbers before ... to specify step. Nest loops for grids. \foreach is provided by pgffor and included automatically with TikZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label mapping in \foreach (value/text pairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow multiple variables separated by / in \foreach, e.g., \x/\xtext, and iterate values as first/second pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lets you keep numeric positions as numeric while using typeset labels (e.g., -0.5/-\frac{1}{2}). If second part omitted, the first is reused as the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Node insertion and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When TikZ encounters the keyword node during path construction, it reads a node specification (options plus text in braces), places the text box at the current position, but nodes are rendered only after the path is completely drawn/filled/shaded/clipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows placement relative to path coordinates and consistent layering. If node directly follows a coordinate, verbatim text inside boxes may be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Node anchors and relative placement options
rubrics_metrics.description: Nodes have anchors (north, south, north east, etc.) to position text relative to a point; options like anchor=north place that anchor on the current position. There are user-friendly shorthands like below, above right, which correspond to anchor names and can take an optional distance (e.g., below=1pt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anchors to place ticks and labels precisely. The semantics can be non-intuitive (anchor=north places the text below the point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Label placement along a path (pos, near start/end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place labels in the middle of a line by adding a node after the --; the pos= option or near start/near end modify the fraction along the path where the label is placed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sloped option to rotate labels to match line slope. Example: -- node[below=2pt] {$\cos\alpha$} (0,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Text width and line breaking in nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit node text width with text width=... so that long explanatory text breaks into lines inside a node box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine with style options (rounded corners, fill=..., inner sep=...) to make readable information boxes in the graphic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve label legibility with label backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use node option fill=white (or other background) to fill the area behind text, preventing interference from the grid or other graphic elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly used for axis tick labels and inline equation labels to improve contrast and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering and layering of drawing commands
rubrics_metrics.description: The order in which \draw/\fill/\shade commands appear determines layering; draw the background elements (e.g., grid) first and important elements last so they appear on top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, use scopes and styles to manage layering and local options.
